question.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2+\text{i},$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-2+\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & -2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} & -2 \\ 5 & 3-\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(-3-\text{i}){x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}+(3-\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(-2+\text{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables to be the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{5}(3-\text{i}){x}_{2}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5}(3-\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-5,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3-\text{i} \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-5}{3-\text{i}}=\frac{-5(3+\text{i})}{10}=-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\text{i}.$
